*Sitting with a cup of tea, thinking about the season ahead...*

Ai, I'm 73 now. Been farming these 4.1 mu for 50 years — my father farmed this same land before me. My wife and I, we're the only ones left at home now. The children work in the city. So it's just us two old ones managing everything.

I do wheat and maize, same as everybody in the village. Wheat goes in October, comes out in June, then straight into maize. No time to rest between — one week, maybe less, to get the maize in the ground after wheat harvest.

**For the wheat that's already in the ground:**

I put down base fertilizer when I planted last October — about one bag of compound fertilizer (50 jin, that's 25 kg) per mu, the 15-15-15 kind from the co-op. Same as always. Now in spring when the wheat starts jointing, I'll topdress with urea, maybe half a bag per mu, around 12-13 kg. If the wheat looks yellow I'll add a bit more. My neighbor Old Wang, he puts more, but he has better soil in his plot.

Irrigation — we have the tube well, share it with three other families. I'll water before winter (already did that), then once at greening-up in March, once at jointing, and once when the grain is filling. That's three or four times. Each time costs money for the electricity — maybe 30-40 yuan per mu each watering. Adds up fast.

For pests — if I see aphids at heading time I'll spray once. Usually need to. Weeds I handle with one herbicide spray in early spring.

I expect maybe 400 kg per mu. Last year was 420, year before was 380. It depends on the rain in May.

**For the maize coming after:**

Soon as the wheat combine leaves, I hire the rotavator man to come — he charges about 40 yuan per mu — then I plant maize right away with a small seeder. I buy hybrid seed, Zhengdan or Xianyu, whatever the shop has. About 30-35 yuan per mu of seed.

Fertilizer for maize — one bag of compound at planting, then urea as topdress when the maize is knee-high. Maybe 30 kg urea per mu total split across the season. If the summer rain is good I won't need to irrigate much; if it's dry in July-August I'll water once or twice.

Maize yield, I usually get 450-500 kg per mu. Last year was a good 480.

**About money and labor:**

Everything is tight. Four mu doesn't give much. We sell maybe half, keep the rest for flour and for feeding the chickens. My wife and I do most of the work ourselves — harvesting I hire the combine for wheat (60 yuan per mu) and for maize (70 yuan per mu). Can't do that by hand at my age anymore.

I don't try to do anything fancy. What worked last year, I do again this year. That's how we've always done it.
